screenGuide.save: Review the information before saving. Required fields are labeled. A success message confirms the change; if a field is invalid, correct the error and try again.

routes.guide: Choose your position. Review how to prepare, work and hand over. Open Training to practice and request a review.
routes.actions: Open your assignment, follow the instructions and submit evidence. Supervisors check the result and record what happens next.
routes.actionsNew: Choose one responsible person below you in the reporting chain, write clear bilingual instructions and set a New York deadline.
routes.0: Review pending confirmations first, then your shift and tasks.
routes.1: Open each shift to see its details. Confirm the published week when requested.
routes.2: Choose a phase and complete your assigned work. Photo tasks ask for evidence before completion.
routes.3: Choose an answer for each question and review the feedback before continuing.
routes.4: Open an item to learn ingredients and allergens. Confirm any changes that need your acknowledgment.
routes.5: Find your assigned tables, read their notes, and use Request for water, clearing or help.
routes.6: Report an item as Low or Out. Your lead or manager handles the next step.
routes.7: Read the rules for your position and confirm each new version.
routes.8: Open an announcement to read it. Confirm it when the sender requests acknowledgment.
routes.9: Use Tools to reach the screens for your role. Your preferences and account controls are below.
routes.10: Assign sections for the open shift, then use the map to review table notes and requests.
routes.11: Review allergy notes by table and seat. Confirm each note after reading it.
routes.12: Review allergy notes and unavailable items before service. Confirm notes after reading them.
routes.13: Publish the service briefing and mark unavailable items. Both expire when the shift closes.
routes.14: Review open shortages and update each item when it is ordered or restocked.
routes.15: Choose a person and a rule that applies to their position. Your manager reviews the proposal.
routes.16: Choose a week, build the shifts and review them before publishing. Published changes notify affected staff.
routes.17: Review all sections before submitting. Filing the close makes this shift read-only.
routes.18: Choose a person to see their position, history and available management actions.
routes.19: Review proposals or issue a warning tied to a valid rule. Only authorized people can see it.
routes.20: Choose the audience, write both languages and decide whether confirmation is required.
routes.21: Select a venue and category, then open or add an item. Review changes before publishing.
routes.22: Review unresolved shortages and mark the action taken for each item.
routes.23: Read the reasons behind the venue state, then open the relevant person or service.
routes.24: Choose a position and phase. Add clear tasks with the weekdays and evidence they require.
routes.25: Choose the rule set, edit both languages and publish a new version for confirmation.
routes.26: Choose a person to manage access and assignments. Share temporary credentials securely.
routes.27: Define named sections and their tables before assigning them during a shift.
routes.28: Choose the menu items available at this venue. Service-only shortages belong in Pre-shift.
routes.29: Choose what you want to configure. Each section explains the records it changes.
routes.30: Open the service to enable operational work. Review the team before starting the close.
routes.31: Explore the reporting chain by area. Instructions go down the chain and reports go up.
routes.32: Read the venue state and its reasons. Open its service details to follow up.
routes.33: Filter the action history to find who changed a record and when.
routes.34: Review the CSV format, upload the schedule and check the preview before importing.
routes.35: Review position names and their place in the supervision chain before saving.
routes.36: Choose a venue to edit its operating details. Save after reviewing the form.
routes.37: Review the operational follow-up rules and save only when the settings match company policy.
routes.38: Create an event with a date, venue and required positions. Staff it from the schedule.
routes.39: Choose a venue, create its sections and tables, then publish a reviewed plan version.
routes.40: Manage shared menu items in both languages, including allergens and photos.
routes.41: Review the operating areas and their names in both languages.
routes.42: Document the written policy and eligible positions. Managers cannot participate in the pool.
routes.43: Choose a company rule set, edit both languages and publish a new version for confirmation.
routes.44: Choose a configuration section. Review venue settings before asking staff to use them.
routes.45: Choose a venue to understand its state and the reasons that need follow-up.
routes.training: Choose a position, practice each criterion and request a supervisor observation.
routes.trainingReview: Read the request, observe the demonstration and record your decision with evidence.
routes.trainingSetup: Edit both languages and publish a new immutable version after reviewing every criterion.

screenGuide.menuAccess: Menu editing and approval follow your position permissions. You can still read the menu or manage venue availability when your role allows it.
